defect.detail: The initial state of selectedProvider uses initialProviders[defaultProvider] (line 214), but contextWindowRef and maxOutputRef (293-299) initialize from providers[0]. When defaultProvider > 0, the Footer reads contextWindowRef.current and displays the wrong context window until the first initClient run corrects both refs — a brief incorrect display on startup.

defect.summary: buildCommandContext hardcodes `permissionMode: () => "default"`, so remote /status always reports "Mode: default" regardless of the actual mode.
defect.detail: The /status handler renders ctx.permissionMode() directly as the current mode, and CommandContext documents the callback as "Returns the current permission mode". The remote server supplies a constant "default" even though the real value handle.permissionMode is in scope two lines above in the same function and is tracked live (plan mode, bypassPermissions after plan approval). A user in plan mode or YOLO mode who runs /status gets factually wrong output; the terminal UI passes the real mode.

defect.summary: A plan approval that arrives while another run is streaming flips the permission mode but silently drops the plan execution.
defect.detail: planApprovalPending is set when a plan-mode run ends with ExitPlanMode success and is only cleared by cancelActiveRun or handlePlanApprovalResponse itself — starting a new run does not reset it. If the user sends an ordinary message after the approval request and the approval response arrives while that run is streaming, handlePlanApprovalResponse proceeds: sets permissionMode to bypassPermissions/prePlanMode, injects the exit reminder, then calls handleUserMessage("Execute this plan:…"), which returns silently on its this.streaming guard. Result: a mode flip to YOLO with no plan run started and no feedback; the "feedback" choice path has the same silent-drop window.

defect.summary: handleResume never broadcasts the new session id, leaving clients with the stale pre-resume session.
defect.detail: restoreRemoteSession replaces handle.sessionId with the resumed session, and the /clear path broadcasts a fresh connected message carrying the new session id, but the /resume path broadcasts only clear, replay messages, a system summary, and command_done. The frontend stores the session id exclusively from the connected message (fe use-chat.ts:149-155) and displays it on the welcome card (welcome.tsx:74), so state.session stays at the pre-resume id. Impact is bounded: the welcome card renders only while the chat is empty, so the stale id is visible mainly after resuming an empty session; the state field is stale regardless for any consumer.

defect.summary: TOCTOU between the duplicate-name check and team.spawnTeammate lets two parallel worktree-isolated Agent calls orphan a teammate
defect.detail: AgentTool has category "read" and no isConcurrencySafe, so partitionToolCalls (agent/index.ts:945-948) batches parallel Agent calls concurrently. In runAsTeammate, the team.getMember(requestedName) check at 448 is separated from team.spawnTeammate at 516 by await createAgentWorktree (493) when isolation="worktree", so two parallel calls with the same name can both pass the check. Team.addMember (teams/index.ts:175-180) unconditionally overwrites the Map entry, orphaning the first member: its in-process loop or external pane keeps polling the same mailbox file and consuming messages, but stopMember/stopAll only see the second entry and its cancel handle/paneId is lost. Without worktree isolation the check-to-spawn path is fully synchronous and safe.

defect.summary: External teammate exits on a shutdown_request without shutdown_response or any leader notification, leaving leader state stuck at "running"
defect.detail: teammate.ts receiving a shutdown request logs and breaks polling (390-393), then exits without sending a shutdown_response or an "[idle] … stopped" message to the leader mailbox. The SendMessageTool schema (teams/tools.ts:230-234) explicitly promises "it replies with shutdown_response"; the in-process loop acks typed requests (teams/index.ts:488-497) but the external path never does. drainLeaderMailbox (which reacts only to "[idle]" messages) never updates the member: uiState stays "running", member.active stays true, and the name stays registered, so subsequent SendMessage calls to the dead teammate vanish silently until someone manually runs TaskStop.

defect.summary: AgentDefinition fields omitMarkdown, skills, memory, and mcpServers are never parsed or consumed anywhere
defect.detail: loader.ts's YamlFrontmatterSchema (92-103) parses none of omit_markdown/skills/memory/mcp_servers, and parseAgentDefinition never sets these fields; a repo-wide search of src/ finds no reader of definition.omitMarkdown, definition.skills, definition.memory, or definition.mcpServers (spawn.ts and prompt/delegation.ts:26-35 use only name, description, initialPrompt, model, tools, disallowedTools, systemPromptOverride, maxTurns, permissionMode, background, isolation). Under the project's zero-dead-code rule these interface fields should be removed or wired up; uncertain only because they may be intentional forward API surface.

defect.summary: loadSession's mtime refresh is not wrapped, so an externally deleted session file turns a successful read into a thrown error
defect.detail: Inside the lock callback, utimesSync(filePath, now, now) runs after all lines are parsed, with no try/catch. The file lock prevents cooperative deletion (cleanExpiredSessions takes the same lock before unlinking), but a non-cooperating deletion (user rm, another tool) between the existsSync check (272) and the utimesSync makes loadSession throw ENOENT and discard the already-parsed messages. The sibling touchSession wraps the identical call in try/catch ("best-effort — the session may not exist (yet)"), showing the failure mode is known; loadSession lacks the same guard.

defect.summary: The raw-import esbuild plugin and the matching `*?raw` ambient declaration in shims.d.ts are unused: no `?raw` import exists anywhere in src/ or tests/
defect.detail: rawImportPlugin (tsup.config.ts:124-136) is registered in both cliConfig.esbuildPlugins and libConfig.esbuildPlugins to mirror Vite-style `?raw` imports, and shims.d.ts:23 declares the `*?raw` module type. A project-wide search for `?raw` across src/ (including src/remote/fe/src) and tests/ finds zero import sites, and vitest supports `?raw` natively without the plugin. Per the repo rule "NEVER maintain dead code... Remove them aggressively", the plugin, its two registrations, and the shim declaration are removable; marked uncertain because it may be kept deliberately as contributor convenience.

defect.summary: globalIgnores lists "app" and "out" directories that do not exist in apps/yukino
defect.detail: eslint.config.js globalIgnores (35-43) ignores "app" and "out" alongside real paths (dist, node_modules, and the three root config files). Neither apps/yukino/app nor apps/yukino/out exists, and no script generates them; the entries appear to be template leftovers. Harmless but stale configuration.

defect.summary: Temp dirs leak into the OS tmpdir in several more test files not covered by the recorded leak defect
defect.detail: Beyond the recorded at-expand/bash-background/clipboard-image/command-loader/consolidation leak, these files also mkdtempSync without rmSync: harness-data.test.ts (workDir factory line 76 + inline workDir() calls), harness-boundaries.test.ts (fixture workDir 57, "outside" dir 206), file-history-rewind.test.ts (makeTempProject 47), file-mailbox.test.ts (per-test mkdtempSync 41,54,72,84,96,108,126,146), history.test.ts (33,52,65), install-skill.test.ts (47,75,86), coordinator.test.ts (per-test workDir 67). Each run leaves dozens of directories in the OS tmpdir.

defect.summary: Fake HOME temp dir created in beforeEach is never removed
defect.detail: beforeEach creates mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "yukino-home-")) and points HOME/USERPROFILE at it; afterEach restores the env vars but never rmSync's the temp home directory, leaking one directory per test. The env-restore logic shows the cleanup intent, so the missing directory removal is an oversight rather than design.

defect.summary: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY env var is deleted only after the assertion, leaking on failure
defect.detail: "falls back to env var" sets process.env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY = "sk-from-env", asserts resolveAPIKey, and deletes the variable only after the expect. If the expectation fails, the delete never runs and the key leaks into every later test in the process. vi.stubEnv with afterEach-style restoration would make the cleanup failure-proof.

defect.summary: Every test creates mkdtempSync work dirs that are never removed
defect.detail: Nine tests call mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "yukino-mem-"/"yukino-malformed-"/"yukino-cap-")) (first at line 83) and write memory files into them, but the file has no afterEach/afterAll rmSync. Sibling files (search-tools, shell-background, skills2, session-recovery-boundaries, prompt-contracts) all clean up, so the convention exists; this file leaks multiple directories per run.

defect.summary: makeTmpDir()/makeCheckerWithTiers temp directories are never removed
defect.detail: makeTmpDir() (line 36) is called by nearly every test, and makeCheckerWithTiers creates two more dirs per call (home + workDir), each with a written .yukino/permissions.yaml; no rmSync exists anywhere in the file. Every run leaks a dozen+ directories with rule files into the OS tmpdir.

defect.summary: Mocked-home and per-test temp directories are never removed
defect.detail: beforeEach (line 63) points mocked os.homedir() at a fresh mkdtempSync dir containing a real config.yaml, and two more tests mkdtemp "yukino-defaults-"/"yukino-invalid-thinking-" dirs (301, 315); there is no afterEach/rmSync, so every run leaks directories with written config files into the OS tmpdir.

defect.summary: makeRepo git-init temp directories are never removed
defect.detail: makeRepo() (line 33) runs mkdtempSync plus git init per call and both tests call it (the second creates a nested tree), but nothing ever removes these directories, leaking git-initialized temp dirs on every run.

defect.summary: Plan test work dir is never removed
defect.detail: Line 51 creates mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "yukino-plan-")) and the test writes a plan file under it; no cleanup exists. Additionally resetPlanPath() mutates module-level global state (only reset at the start of that test), which persists across the rest of the run.

defect.summary: ctx() creates a fresh work dir per test that is never removed
defect.detail: Every one of the five tests calls ctx() which runs mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "yukino-rf-img-")) and writes image/text fixture files into it; there is no afterEach/afterAll rmSync, so five directories per run accumulate in the OS tmpdir.

defect.summary: makeContext() work dirs are never removed
defect.detail: makeContext() (line 59) creates a fresh mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "yukino-ps-bg-")) for each of the seven tests (each spawning real pwsh processes with that cwd), and nothing removes them; directories leak on every run on platforms where pwsh is available.

defect.summary: Per-test home and work temp dirs are never removed, including the multi-hundred-KB configs from the atomic-config test
defect.detail: beforeEach (46-53) mkdtemps a fake HOME per test and workDir() (69) mkdtemps a project dir per call; afterEach (55-67) only restores env vars and never rmSync's either. Twelve tests each leave a home dir (with .yukino/teams contents) plus one or more work dirs. The atomic-config test (305) persists a ~256 KB description and leaves the final config plus its reader-stop file on disk. The sibling pattern in teammate-mode.test.ts (rmSync in afterEach) shows cleanup is the project norm.

defect.summary: Every test mkdtemps a work dir holding spill files (up to 250 KB) that is never deleted
defect.detail: Each of the eleven tests creates mkdtempSync(join(tmpdir(), "yukino-tr-")) and applyBudget/persistLargeResult write spill files into .yukino/sessions/s/tool-results/ (the "spills rich text" test writes a 250 KB file); no afterEach exists, so all directories persist in the OS tmpdir. The identical pattern exists in tests/tool-result-wiring.test.ts (yukino-wire-/yukino-wire-img- dirs, lines 129,178,205,231,261,341), and smaller instances of the same leak appear in tests/todo.test.ts, tests/teams.test.ts, tests/teams-shared-task.test.ts, tests/team-protocol.test.ts, and tests/teammate-registry.test.ts.

defect.summary: "lists the available tools" only asserts one of the two registered candidates
defect.detail: The test registers mcp__linear__create_issue and mcp__jira__create_issue, dispatches with server "nope", and asserts the error output contains only "mcp__linear__create_issue". The implementation joins all available names (src/tools/mcp-call.ts:280), but if a regression dropped the second candidate from the listing, the test would still pass despite the title claiming the tools (plural) are listed.

defect.summary: `expect(level).toBe("high")` asserts against a const binding that can never change, so the assertion is vacuous
defect.detail: In "does not save after a runtime setter failure" (118), level is declared const ThinkingLevel = "high" and the throwing setThinkingLevel cannot mutate it, so the final expect passes unconditionally no matter what the handler does. The same assertion is meaningful in the clamp test at 141, where level is let and the setter reassigns it. The test's other assertions (persistThinkingLevel not called, output text) still cover the contract, so impact is cosmetic, but the assertion as written cannot detect any regression.

defect.summary: Removed eight trailing comments on SKIP_DIRS entries that merely restated well-known directory names
defect.detail: Deleted `// Git`, `// Yukino`, `// Next.js`, `// Python venv`, `// Python mypy`, `// Python`, `// Webpack, Vite`, `// Node.js` from the SKIP_DIRS set entries; no code changed.

defect.summary: Removed a comment in the timeout handler that merely restated the adjacent auto-background/terminate branches.
defect.detail: Deleted "// Auto-background on timeout when allowed; otherwise hard-kill."; the code (autoBackgroundAllowed && backgroundExecution("timeout") vs terminate()) is self-explanatory.

defect.summary: Removed a comment restating the file-state-cache gate check.
defect.detail: Deleted "// Gate: read-before-edit enforcement." above the ctx.fileStateCache.check(filePath) block; the code and gate.error message already convey it.

defect.summary: Removed the false claim that the jq exit codes follow its manual.
defect.detail: Changed "// jq is a local JSON processor, not a network tool; codes per its manual" to "// jq is a local JSON processor, not a network tool" because the mapped code 5 contradicts the jq manual. The incorrect mapping itself is reported as a separate new defect.

defect.summary: Removed one comment that merely restated the statement it preceded.
defect.detail: Deleted "// Rebuild the visible transcript from the restored records." above `const resumedMessages = transcriptFromRestored(restored);` in the /resume handler — the function name and its JSDoc already convey this.

defect.summary: Comment claimed the getDraft() re-read guards only against uncommitted pastes
defect.detail: Line 553: "preceding paste" corrected to "preceding edit" — the stale-closure guard applies to every edit type (typing, cursor moves, paste), consistent with text-field.tsx:139.

defect.summary: Comment overclaimed report retention across the escape-flush timeout
defect.detail: Lines 105-108: replaced "Once a report has started, retain it across the theme timeout" with the actual rule — pending bytes are flushed after the 25 ms timeout unless a paste is in progress or the buffer already starts with a full report prefix (retained until complete, including an ST terminator split at ESC / \).

defect.summary: Removed a comment that merely restated the adjacent constant names and regex literals.
Module header claimed the port avoids pulling zod into the browser bundle, but zod is bundled via types.ts.
defect.detail: Replaced "without pulling zod into the browser bundle" with "implemented without zod": types.ts imports zod (ServerMessageSchema) and is bundled into the browser build through use-chat.ts/use-web-socket.ts with no `external` entries in the fe tsup config. Remaining claims verified accurate and kept.

defect.summary: Fixed one misleading JSDoc and removed four redundant restatement comments in the remote server.
defect.detail: (1) currentAgent JSDoc claimed "the agent of the current run, if any" although the reference intentionally survives run completion for takeSteeringLeftovers() post-run draining — reworded to "current or most recent run … mid-run steering and post-run leftover draining". (2) Deleted restatements: "Static file serving for fe/dist/", "Pending permission/ask-user requests waiting for WS client responses", "With arguments: send to agent loop", "Clear UI and replay messages".

defect.summary: Fixed a misleading catch-block comment and removed three redundant method comments
defect.detail: readAll's catch comment claimed "one bad record should not block the entire teammate" but the catch handles whole-file corruption (single bad records are dropped by the safeParse filter) — reworded; deleted restating comments on receiveSync, unreadCount, and markAllRead.

defect.summary: The resolve-closure comment described a control-flow short-circuit that does not occur, conflating two distinct positioning steps.
defect.detail: Old comment claimed "a successful re-location overwrites existing_code … short-circuiting the deterministic cross-file probe," but relocateWithLlm (the step that overwrites existing_code) runs after relocateAcrossFiles, so it cannot short-circuit it. Replaced with the accurate ordering rationale: the deterministic cross-file probe runs before the side-effecting LLM step so it gets first chance to locate the comment without overwriting existing_code.
